status: found by reproducing the filing in the build session; each is a question for the petitioner and the reviewer — none is resolved by the build

findings.title: F25 / F26 FY2023-24 do not use F14's capitalisation
findings.detail: F26 adds equity of 21.21 and F25 a normative loan of 49.49 in the FY2023-24 "Claimed" column; the same filing's F14 gives 30 % / 70 % of its net capitalisation, 22.73 / 53.04.  F26 retires no equity that year; F14 retires 1.53.

findings.title: Receivables: the Commission and the petitioner use different bases
findings.detail: NPCL's projection takes 1.5 months of tariff and open-access revenue; the Commission's FY2025-26 approval (as F27 restates it) takes tariff revenue alone (370.25 × 12 / 1.5 = 2,962.0).  True-up years use billing (FY2022-23 grossed up by 1.0473).

findings.title: F18 prints its ARR column as FY 2025-26
findings.detail: The WPI format's last column is headed "FY 2025-26" like the APR column before it; F17 heads the same column "FY 2026-27".

findings.title: Carrying cost on a surplus: full rate (Commission) or 75 % of a deposit rate (NPCL)
findings.detail: The Commission's approvals, as NPCL restates them, carry a surplus at the full carrying rate (FY2024-25: × 11.05 %, Rs 122.34 crore); NPCL's own columns at 75 % of a deposit rate (6.75 %; 6.5 % for FY2026-27) — Rs 56.05 crore for the same base.

findings.title: Depreciation: land on a base excluding land rights; one office-equipment year
findings.detail: NPCL depreciates land at 3.34 % of the average gross block less the non-depreciable land rights (3.99); FY2024-25 office equipment (pre-2020 assets) is 0.5373 where the class rate gives 0.5073.

findings.title: F24 FY2023-24: the rate column divides by the net block
findings.detail: The FY2023-24 block's "Applicable rate" (J38:J56) is G / ((B − F) + (C − D) / 2) — the year's depreciation over the opening gross block less accumulated depreciation; the FY2024-25 to FY2026-27 blocks divide by the gross block (B + (C − D) / 2), and FY2022-23 prints the rate itself.  Land therefore shows 3.67 % in FY2023-24 against 3.34 % in the other years.  The depreciation figures are unaffected; the printed rates are not comparable across years.

findings.title: Depreciation of the APR and ARR years: the computation is not in the filing
findings.detail: F24 types each class's depreciation for FY2025-26 and FY2026-27.  Annexure-21 rolls only the existing assets forward (gross 111.39 for FY2025-26 against F24's 121.04).  The excess fits half a year at the class rate on the year's additions for land, buildings, vehicles and metering (0.50), but about 0.40 for lines & cables, plant & machinery and communication equipment in FY2025-26, and no single fraction in FY2026-27.  Consumer-contribution depreciation is 30.94 in F24 against 29.65 in the workings.  The totals reproduce from F24's class figures (net 90.09 and 106.75, as the ARR carries); the class figures themselves cannot be derived from what was filed.  Ask for the working, e.g. additions by month or by funding source.

findings.title: Interest on security deposit, FY2024-25: March typed, not computed
findings.detail: F30 computes each month's interest as the month's average deposit × 6.75 % / 12; March (M10) is typed as 1.8901 where the formula gives 2.0802.  The year's total is therefore 24.79 (carried to F30A, F25 row 16 and the ARR's row 38) where the monthly balances give 24.98.  The claim is 0.19 below the computation — it reads as the interest actually disbursed with March as the balancing month; the petitioner should say so, and the reviewer should allow the amount disbursed, not the computation.

findings.title: ESR-3 FY2024-25: a typed 0.04 in the regulatory-discount total
findings.detail: The total regulatory discount N136 is SUM(N12:N135) − 0.04 (−288.18 against the rows' −288.14), while the revenue total O136 sums the rows' totals, which carry no such adjustment.  So the discount column and the revenue total disagree by Rs 0.04 crore; the revenue the ARR carries (2,634.60) is the rows' sum.  The petitioner should say what the 0.04 is.
where: ESR_3 Curr Tariff FY25 N136, O136

findings.title: Urban domestic revenue implies rates 1.8–1.9 % below the schedule in force
findings.detail: ESR-3 FY2026-27's rural domestic slabs bill exactly the existing tariff of ESR4A (3.35, 3.85, 5.00, 5.50 Rs/kWh).  The urban domestic slabs imply 5.396, 5.398, 5.891 and 6.386 Rs/kWh against 5.50, 5.50, 6.00 and 6.50, i.e. 1.76–1.89 % lower, by a different fraction in each slab.  Fixed charges do not reduce to load × rate either: rural metered, 49.46 MW × Rs 90 / kW / month × 12 = 5.34 crore against 4.10 billed.  The revenue at current tariff (the ARR's row 15) therefore cannot be computed from the rate schedule alone.  Ask the petitioner for the rebates, the load basis and the slab mix behind ESR-3.
where: ESR_3 Curr Tariff FY27 G23:G26, J13
ESR4A_Prop Tariff Rate Sch. C16:C20, C34:C37

findings.title: Formats: one listed and not filed, two blank, one indexed twice, one not indexed
findings.detail: The workbook's own index lists 74 formats.  ESR7 (BD monthly — the monthly billing determinants) has no sheet in the workbook.  ESR6 (revenue from tariff subsidy) and F10 (bulk supply tariff details) are blank: the petitioner should say whether they are nil or omitted.  F22 for FY2026-27 is listed twice ('FY 26' and 'FY 26 and FY 27'); one sheet covers both.  F19A (normative O&M) is filed but not in the index.  This accounts against the petitioner's index, not yet against the Commission's list of mandatory formats, which is not among the documents.

findings.title: Power purchase: the claim is 1.50 below the reconciliation with the audited accounts
findings.detail: Annexure-14 bridges the audited accounts (Note 46(b): net charges 2,093.62, transmission 294.40) to the true-up claim: less 36.94 booked in FY2024-25 but claimed in another year, plus 120.46 of earlier years' claims = 2,471.54.  PPC FY 25 claims 2,470.04 (the ARR's rows 20 + 22 + 23).  The 1.50 is the carrying cost for FY2023-24: 12.88 in the reconciliation, 11.37 in PPC FY 25 (row 77).  The split between the year's sources and the arrears also differs by 8.77 — the 10 % of FY2022-23 and FY2023-24 additional coal booked in FY2024-25, inside the accounts' base in the annexure and among the arrears in PPC — which nets to nothing.  Which carrying cost is right?

findings.title: BS1 (profit and loss) is built from the ARR format, not taken from the audited accounts
findings.detail: Every figure of BS1 is a formula over the ARR format (revenue = ARR row 17, power purchase = rows 20–24, employee = row 29, finance costs = rows 37–40 and 45 less 62, depreciation = row 36, tax = row 44) or over F22 / F23.  It restates the claim as a profit and loss account; it is not evidence that the claim agrees with the audited accounts.  The reviewer should reconcile the true-up year to the audited accounts (Annexure-1(a)) and the trial balance (Annexure-41) themselves.  Annexure-14 does so for power purchase only (A44).

findings.title: Employee expenses claimed exceed the trial balance by exactly Rs 0.0105 crore
findings.detail: The trial balance's employee benefits expense (Note 30, 19 accounts before capitalisation) is 95.409346859 crore; F21 claims 95.419846859 — exactly 0.0105 crore (Rs 1.05 lakh) more, every other digit equal, so one typed component differs by that amount.  Capitalisation agrees (17.19), so net employee expenses (the ARR's row 29) are 78.23 claimed against 78.22 in the books.  Everything else checked against the trial balance agrees to the paisa of a crore: power purchase and transmission net of rebate, interest on security deposit (24.79, which supports A40's reading), finance charges, bad debts written off, loss on retired assets.  Which F21 line carries the 0.0105?

findings.title: F32: the ARR summary column double-counts interest; the allocation base is not the net ARR
findings.detail: F32's 'ARR summary' column (L) adds the net interest line (L16 = ARR rows 37–40, 119.31) and also its parts (L17, L18): its ARR is 3,692.18 where the allocated columns give 3,572.87 — 119.31 counted twice.  Only the allocated columns (F, H) feed the cross-subsidy surcharge (F33), so the double count does not reach it.  The allocated base itself is not the net ARR (3,481.83): it adds the regulatory assets' carrying cost (83.23, F33's R), leaves out provisions (3.00) and does not deduct other-business income and open-access revenue (10.82).  The reviewer should decide the base the cost of supply for the surcharge is computed on.

findings.title: RPO: losses and sales not the filing's own; obligations netted across categories
findings.detail: F6 brings renewable purchases to the distribution periphery with transmission losses typed into its formulas: 3.58 % inter-state and 3.18 % intra-state for FY2025-26 and FY2026-27, where the Energy Balance has 3.55 % / 3.30 % (FY2025-26) and 3.41 % / 3.35 % (FY2026-27); for FY2024-25 3.46875 % / 3.20862 % against 3.46868 % / 3.21055 %.  Its sales differ from ESR-3 by about 0.004 MU each year (3,597.6329 against 3,597.6293 for FY2024-25).  The year's obligation adds the solar, non-solar and hydro balances, so a surplus in one category (FY2026-27 solar −154.32 MU, non-solar −134.81 MU) offsets a shortfall in another (hydro +141.88 MU), and a net surplus (−147.25 MU) is carried forward as a credit.  FY2025-26's REC purchase is typed equal to that year's obligation (215.12 MU).  The reviewer should decide whether categories are fungible and whether a surplus carries forward; the petitioner should use the Energy Balance's losses.

findings.title: PPC FY 24: figures adjusted by hand inside their formulas, and an unlabelled amount
findings.detail: In the FY2023-24 power purchase summary: change in law for FY2020-21 is 4.85790 − 0.05 (N66); the carrying cost on the long-term claims is 1.17434 × 0 + 0.89 (N68) — computed, zeroed and replaced by a typed 0.89; the carrying cost on the medium-term claims is 0.88151 × 0 (M75, P75); the FY2023-24 incentive (2.66577) is multiplied by 0 (M11, Q11); and row 79 carries 0.0743 with no label into the transmission arrears (R80, the ARR's row 24).  The totals reproduce from the figures as entered; the adjustments themselves are not explained.  Ask the petitioner for the reason of each.
where: PPC FY 24 M11, N66, N68, M75, P75, row 79

findings.title: Distribution loss: P1_DL claims more than the petition is computed at
findings.detail: P1_DL's 'Claimed' column gives 7.45 % for FY2025-26 and 7.42 % for FY2026-27 (and 7.40 %, 7.38 %, 7.37 % for the next control period, against the Commission's 6.70 %, 6.43 %, 6.16 %).  The Energy Balance and the ARR format — and so the power purchase, sales and ARR — use 7.23 % and 6.97 %, the Commission's approved losses.  For FY2024-25 P1_DL's 7.479277 % differs from the Energy Balance's 7.479214 % in the sixth decimal.  Which loss does NPCL claim?  If it claims P1_DL's, the energy requirement and the power purchase of the APR and ARR years are understated; if the approved, P1_DL should say so.
